correctness.rationale: The projection is piecewise affine; each full-dimensional active-set derivative pools vertices in connected equal-level components, hence cyclic intervals on C_n. For uniform edge weights sample an independent representative in each block according to the observation masses: its blockwise constant vector has expectation equal to the block-averaging derivative. The clockwise paths connecting representatives partition the cycle, giving the sample variation at most original variation; Jensen and derivative integration prove global two-input contraction. Every Hasse cover edge can be uniquely pooled on a full-dimensional neighborhood by identifying its endpoints and assigning a strict quotient-poset rank; otherwise it would be transitively redundant. Applying the pooling derivative to h_{i−1}=h_i=1,h_{i+1}=h_{i+2}=0 yields V_w(E_ih)−V_w(h)=[a_{i+1}w_{i−1}+a_iw_{i+1}]/(a_i+a_{i+1})−w_i. At a minimum edge weight, global contraction forces both neighbors equal, propagating uniformity. Nonuniform weights force one positive gain, realized by arbitrarily close actual input pairs. n≥4 and positivity hypotheses ensure valid distinct test coordinates/strict convex combination.

value.rationale: A complete rigidity boundary for a natural non-chain poset family and two independent weighting systems, with a sharp small diamond counterexample. This determines when isotonic fitting preserves a practically meaningful graph total-variation distance, not merely re-labeling a chain result.

limitations: No classification for arbitrary Hasse graphs, general convex loss or nonuniform norm magnitude; only strict amplification is proven for nonuniform weights.
